metadata.title: Strawberry shortcake
metadata.description:
Make this decadent dessert this Labor Day weekend. It's so easy to make but your guest won't believe it's homemade. Recipe as follows:

Cake
1 1/3 cups of AP flour
2/3 cups of sugar
1 egg
1 tsp of vanilla extract
2 tsp of baking powder
1/2 tsp of baking soda
1/4 tsp of salt
4 tbsp of melted butter

Topping
1/2 cup of strawberry preserves
1 tbsp of water
1 tbsp of lemon juice (fresh squeezed)
1 lb of fresh strawberries (hulled and cut into eights)
1/2 tsp of kosher salt
1 tbsp of sugar

Whipped cream
1 1/2 cups of heavy whipping cream
1/4 cup of sugar
1/2 tsp of vanilla extract

#strawberryshortcake #foodlovewithanna #recipe

nodes.plm_caption:
This video features a Montage of a pair of hands, making strawberries shortcake cupcakes.  Throughout the video the hands are shown demonstrating how to put together cupcakes and strawberries on a plate. The video has a Foodlove logo at the beginning.
The background is light wood with the video on a solid black screen over the Foodlove logo.

There are bright, natural colors throughout the video.

summary.brief: Hands prepare batter, bake mini shortcakes, whip cream, macerate strawberries, and assemble strawberry shortcake cupcakes with lemon garnish and mint.
summary.detailed: The video opens with the Foodlove logo and a pair of hands measuring flour, sugar, salt, baking powder and baking soda into a single bowl, then adding an egg, melted butter, vanilla extract and milk before mixing everything with a hand‑mixer into a thick batter. The batter is poured into a greased, floured mini‑cake pan and baked at 350 °F for about 20 minutes until golden, then set aside to cool completely. While the cakes cool, fresh strawberries are quartered, tossed with granulated sugar and a pinch of kosher salt, and left to macerate. Heavy whipping cream is beaten with powdered sugar and vanilla until soft peaks form and then chilled. Strawberry preserves are warmed with a little water and fresh lemon juice, stirred, and combined with the macerated berries to create a glossy strawberry topping. For assembly, each cooled shortcake is sliced horizontally; the bottom half receives a dollop of whipped cream, a spoonful of the strawberry topping, and then the top half (the “bun”) is placed back on. The assembled cupcakes are finished with extra strawberry pieces, a drizzle of the strawberry‑preserve sauce, a few lemon wedges placed on the side, and a fresh mint leaf on top. The segment concludes with on‑screen prompts to like, comment, and subscribe.

action.detailed: Using a pair of hands, split each cooled shortcake, spread whipped cream on the bottom half, spoon strawberry topping over the cream, replace the top half, then garnish with additional strawberries, a drizzle of sauce, lemon wedges, and a mint leaf.

summary.brief: The video shows hands measuring, mixing, and baking shortcake batter, then preparing a strawberry topping and whipped‑cream frosting for a strawberry shortcake.
summary.detailed: The clip begins with the FoodLove logo and a hand measuring flour, sugar, salt, baking powder, baking soda, an egg, melted butter, vanilla extract and milk into a bowl, then mixing everything with a hand‑mixer until a thick batter forms. The batter is poured into a greased and floured pan that makes small individual round cakes, baked at 350 °F for about twenty minutes until golden brown, and set aside to cool completely. Fresh strawberries are quartered and then halved to release their juice, tossed with granulated sugar and a pinch of kosher salt, and left to macerate. Heavy whipping cream is placed in a large bowl, beaten with the hand‑mixer, powdered sugar and vanilla extract are added, and the mixture is whipped to soft peaks, covered and chilled. All of these preparations occur within the first 160 seconds of the video.

action.detailed: Measure and combine the flour, sugar, salt, baking powder, baking soda, egg, melted butter, vanilla extract and milk in a bowl, mix with a hand‑mixer until thick, pour the batter into a greased, floured pan of small round molds, bake at 350 °F for about twenty minutes, let the cakes cool, quarter and halve fresh strawberries and toss them with sugar and kosher salt to macerate, beat heavy whipping cream with a hand‑mixer, add powdered sugar and vanilla, whip to soft peaks, then cover and chill the whipped cream.

summary_sent_to_llm.description:
Make this decadent dessert this Labor Day weekend. It's so easy to make but your guest won't believe it's homemade. Recipe as follows:

Cake
1 1/3 cups of AP flour
2/3 cups of sugar
1 egg
1 tsp of vanilla extract
2 tsp of baking powder
1/2 tsp of baking soda
1/4 tsp of salt
4 tbsp of melted butter

Topping
1/2 cup of strawberry preserves
1 tbsp of water
1 tbsp of lemon juice (fresh squeezed)
1 lb of fresh strawberries (hulled and cut into eights)
1/2 tsp of kosher salt
1 tbsp of sugar

Whipped cream
1 1/2 cups of heavy whipping cream
1/4 cup of sugar
1/2 tsp of vanilla extract

#strawberryshor

While the cakes cool, fresh strawberries are quartered, tossed with granulated sugar and a pinch of kosher salt, and left to macerate. Heavy whipping cream is beaten with powdered sugar and vanilla until soft peaks form and then chilled. Strawberry preserves are warmed with a little water and fresh lemon juice, stirred, and combined with the macerated berries to create a glossy strawberry topping. For assembly, each cooled shortcake is sliced horizontally; the bottom half receives a dollop of whipped cream, a spoonful of the strawberry topping, and then the top half (the “bun”) is placed back on. The assembled cupcakes are finished with extra strawberry pieces, a drizzle of the strawberry‑preserve sauce, a few lemon wedges placed on the side, and a fresh mint leaf on top.
